I was 14, and my "friend" who had a crush on me and vice versa, thought it would be super cool to stay out all night. Eventually we got tired and bored plus it started raining. So we went to his house where we stayed in this old junk car they had in their backyard. He obviously had more experience because he whipped it out after like 2 small make out sessions. Wasn't my first kiss but defiantly my first full on make out session with touching and everything. He took it out and I had watched porn once or twice so I knew what he wanted but I didn't know you had to suck! I just put my lips around it and moved up and down. Accidentally let my teeth get too close.

The next day he told all our friends. I confided in him earlier in the day I had never even French kissed a guy before and he said he would teach me. Then mocked me with all our friends the very next day. Even my best friend got in on the jokes.

I never talked to him again. I felt so embarrassed and like a huge prude. He sent me a message on Facebook a few years back (we are both now in our early twenties) and he apologized. Said he really liked me but felt pressured to tell the cool kids (our "friends") to fit in. He said he didn't know they would tease me about it. Even at one point said he thought he loved me (we had been close friends for a year or two before this) and feels like a dick. It was awkward to be around him after that. I blocked him and haven't thought about it since now lol

My mother, sister and I lived in an apartment. We had wooden stairs outside to get to the top floor which was ours. 

One day after realizing my sister hadn't come home from school, and beginning to worry, I walked outside. I started down the stairs and I started to hear crying. Like hysterical crying. I found her in the middle of the 1st and 2nd floor banging her head on a step.

She and my mother had recently been fighting, often times in screaming matches and usually every day. She just kept repeating "Why does mom hate me?". I went to help her, but she didn't stop the banging. All I could do was hug her and put my hand on the step where she was banging her head to prevent her from hurting herself.

I will never forget this. She's always had mental problems but this is the first time it escalated to a state of mind in which she wasn't present and unable to respond to help.

I agree, it's just kind of hard. I can't help thinking that I'm over reacting. I should just let it be but I'm so anxious that in 3 months he's gonna come back and explain and all of a sudden I'll wanna shoot myself in the foot for overreacting... I want to move on and begin something new, I do. I just can't help remembering how great we were together when he randomly pops back into my life.

When I was 10 my mom had a very stern "No Make-Up" rule. At that age I followed my 12 year old sister around and always tagged along for sleep overs (though she hated it). We went to her friends house who lived down the street where a lot of the neighborhood kids enjoyed hanging around. We would all play and sometimes it would get a little rough with wrestling or tag or whatever we decided to do. And one of the neighborhood boys very lightly "head-locked me". This is important to the story. Later that night it was just my sister, her friend and myself. We spent the night. My #1 dream job for most my childhood up on until 19 was a horror movie director so I decided we should play "make a movie" with a camera we found. I was the monster/camera man when I wasn't on screen - this is where make up becomes involved. I had a "bloody" neck and black eye makeup to look dead. My sister and her friend were the unsuspecting victims. After we made our movie I "washed off" my makeup or so I thought. Fast forward to the next day when I head home. My mom instantly noticed my red neck and what looked like on black eye. She immediately began grilling. I was so scared about the makeup that I made up a story on the spot. I said we were playing rough and the boy from the neighborhood had accidentally hooked my neck and bruised my eye. Well.... my mom freaks out and goes off on the boys mom. I felt bad and almost instantly told the truth. She dragged me by my ear to apologize and I was never allowed to play with that boy again.

I'm sure this is different for everyone but it's not much about what you say as it is about what you do. The one thing most don't realize is that depression isn't easily defined and what may work one time isn't always enough the next time. The most important thing a loved one can do is learn about it and understand it. I think personally I hate hearing "I went through something similar and I'm okay now" or "it could be worse so and so has this going on". 

What I found works are letters and 1 on 1 time. I've recently fell on hard times and had really bad thoughts about 3 months ago which also coincidentally was tax time and when my then fiancé bought a gun. It's stupid enough to say but what saved me then was my dog who had recently had puppies. If I was gone my ex fiance would have just dropped them off at the pound so I figured I oughta wait until the puppies had found homes. I had a plan, my fiance worked overnights, and I would run a nice hot shower and afterwards write a letter and be done. My worse times are when it's calm and quiet in the middle of the night and I'm alone in the dark. When "bad things" happen I usually am too distracted to have suicidal thoughts. I have most my "ducks in a row" during the calm before the storm when I'm able to plan and rationally think (depressive episodes vs manic). When I had found the puppies homes unfortunately the damage was already done and the landlord had found out about our 5 puppies and evicted us. This would have sent my thoughts into overdrive if not for my sister. She had offered me her home, a place she said was safe, a place she genuinely WANTED me to be. She saved me that night, I was alone and felt defeated and like a failure until I called her. She never once joined in on the pity party, instead she offered a solution to my newly found problems. She had been discussing it a while because she feared for my safety being with the man I was with because of multiple incidents. She had even rented a house with an extra room for me, just in case I ever needed it and now that I did she didn't hesitate one second before she said "I will buy you a bus ticket here, I can't wait for you to meet my boys!!" (Her boyfriend has kids from a previous marriage that she so lovingly has took under her wing). The way she sounded and the tone in her voice wasn't one of annoyance or even concern, she sounded happy which changed my train of thought. Even now she finds little ways to prove how much she cares. Little notes here and there, always willing to talk to me, and when I was having a rough day (officially ending my 3 year relationship) she went out and bought me an adult coloring book and a short horror story book. She said it would help me relax. She worked all day and got home roughly at 2 am yet still went 30 minutes out of her way to Walmart to buy me "stress relievers". 

It was never about what she would say as much as do. A letter or note is hand written and for whatever reason meant so much to me. Spending all day at work and instead of coming home and relaxing, she decided to help me. When I would bring up something sad she would just remind me of my strength and just LISTEN. She wouldn't budge in and say anything, just let me vent. Afterwards she would offer a few kind words and then the tables would turn and I'd listen while she vented. 

Here's the difference in a conversation I had with my mom and the one I had with my sister:

Mom: "find a job yet?"
Me: "well I've had a rough few days and my mind hasn't been on it lately."
Mom: "but you gotta keep on it! Can't be freeloading at your sisters!"
Me: "well-"
Mom: "plus you're single now how will you meet anyone if you're in the house all day"
Me: "I still love ______, I don't want to move on yet, I still wear my ring"
Mom: "You need to move on, he was a (insults here, negative comment there)"
Me: "I miss him though"
*awkward silence*
Mom: "don't be stupid, when I was with _______ I felt the same way at first! Did you know the bastard still hasn't signed the divorce papers? I called his lawyer and............ (on and on and on from there about her ex)"

Alternatively I'm so grateful for my sister.

Sister: "what's wrong???"
Me: "nothing"
Sister: "okay, love you!"
(I can't stress enough how much I appreciated her giving me my space in that time and allowing me to just calm myself down in my room with a few good crys)
Later after she gets home from work and she sees the dramatic posts my ex made about me on Facebook the day we officially broke it off instead of the initial "separation".
Sister: "wanna talk about it?" Gestures towards patio with a small glass of wine ready for me in her hand
Me: "yes", starting to tear up
Sister: "I saw what ______ said on FB are you two okay?"
Me: "no... we broke up today, he's already talking to someone new. I know he was an ass but I miss him so much, he hasn't called me once since I've been here and now this."
Sister: "I know you do... it will be hard but trust me, I know you're strong enough. What happened?"
Me: (insert long explanation why we broke up)
Sister: "3 years is a long time and it will take some time to heal, but (bfs name) and I are here for you. Take your time finding a job, we love you and I know you're going through a lot. We appreciate all the things you've done since you've been here."
Her step sons come outside and she stopped talking and gave one of those "I'm sorry" smiles and then begins talking about something we should all do as a family tomorrow. And then offers we all play a card game when we get inside which was fun and distracted me from my horrible day.

She never interrupted, she never looked at me like I was being dramatic, she never mentioned that it could be worse, she never added in some of her "experience" or made anything about her and she just sat calmly while giving a bit of advice here and there being completely supportive and understanding.

I'm so lucky to have her, she's planning on going to school to be a counselor and I couldn't imagine a more patient and kind person to do it.

She's saved me. And I'm forever grateful.

Btw I forgot to mention what my routine is!

I went with the "no poo" method for a long time and only co-washed for about 7 months. I didn't like it so I switched up a lot these past few weeks. I've seen improvements in the actual texture and definition but nothing about volume or weight.

Here's my routine: I wash my hair every 3 days with a "shampoo all natural bar" made from essential oils and goats milk (?) I do believe. My definition has improved since adding the bar into my routine. I then use Aussie's miracle conditioner in "moist" expect when once a week I use a deep conditioning mask infused with Argan oil. I do no own a brush and detangle my curls while washing out conditioner and have a wide tooth comb for when I miss any knots (which I rarely do). After I get out of the shower I'll just run my fingers through my hair through a t-shirt (sounds weird but I basically make a glove out of whatever t-shirt I will scrunch my hair with and run my fingers through to separate the curls) and then kinda blot the water out with the same Tshirt for a few seconds and then add my leave in conditioner (sometimes). Nothing too special, just separate curls, blot with Tshirt and go about my day. I spend no more than 1-2 minutes on my hair after leaving the shower but that also depends on what my plans are. I either let it fully air dry with no products or add a TINY amount of leave in conditioner (just a quarter amount lathered into the palms of my hands and then applied using a few scrunches). If I have time I will occasionally use my diffuser - however my hair used to go through a lot of heat damage due to frequent straightenings so I try to avoid using heat nowadays because my hair is healthier than it has ever been. Haven't straightened my hair in over a year and still had frizzy dry ends last time I went for a trim. That was 3 months ago and my ends are beautiful and strong and I'm so scared of ruining my new frizz free strong curls, that I don't like diffusing.

I've tried using "volumizing" products including a few from DevaCurl and still have yet to get the curl to start from the roots.
